_comment: THE REGISTRY, and it is the only source of truth about what this machine can do.
A tool that is not in this file does not exist. The brain is shown the capability
sentences and nothing else; it asks for a tool by id with a control tag; and the id
it names is looked up here EXACTLY - no fuzzy match, no nearest name, no guessing at
a near neighbour. That is the same discipline as the model allowlist, for the same
reason: a machine that guesses which action you meant will one day guess wrong while
holding something sharp.
No key, token or password ever appears here, and none is ever passed to a script. A
tool that needs a credential reads config.json itself, server-side, and the wire
between this machine and the browser never carries one.
Each entry:
id          the name the brain asks for and the ledger counts under. [a-z0-9_-]
name        what a human calls it, shown above the Yes/No pair
script      a bare filename inside tools/ - never a path, never a shell string
capabilities the sentences the brain may match a request against. Write them the
way your employer would say the thing, not the way a manual would.
triggers    regular expressions that decide only ONE thing: whether a message is
worth offering the brain a chance to ask for hands at all. They never
choose a tool - the brain does that, and the id above is checked
exactly. A trigger that is too greedy costs a model call; a trigger
that is too narrow means the hands are never offered.
params      name / type / required. string, text, integer, number, boolean.
Anything not listed here is dropped before the script sees it.
timeout_s   how long it may run before it is killed and reported as failed
proposal    the sentence spoken before anything happens, with {param} blanks.
This is where your voice lives: write it the way you would want to be
asked. It is composed from THIS template and never from model prose,
because a model that paraphrases an action can understate it.
Adding a hand is a ten-line script and four lines of JSON. Nothing else.

tools.name: Write something into the calendar
capabilities: put an appointment, a reminder or a meeting in the employer's calendar
remind the employer to do something at a particular time
book or schedule something for a given day or hour
tools.proposal: That would be '{title}' at {when}, sir, written into your calendar. Shall I put it in?

tools.name: Send an email
capabilities: send an email to somebody on the employer's behalf
write to a person or an address and say something to them
tools.proposal: I have an email ready for {to}, sir, under the subject '{subject}'. Shall I send it?

tools.name: Test the hands themselves
capabilities: prove that the tool machinery itself works, touching nothing at all
tools.proposal: A self test, sir, carrying the token {token} and touching nothing. Shall I run it?
